title: Game Math Part 2 · 3D Rotation 3: Understanding and Computing Quaternions

scenes.title: 이번 강의에서 배울 것
lines: How can four numbers record an airborne rotation in a game?
We will observe ski and bike orientations, then visualize the four quaternion components and their half-angle.
We will undo and compose rotations, and compute the difference between two orientations.
Finally, we will check sign and normalization pitfalls and rotate a vector in a worked exercise.

scenes.title: 스키의 이동과 자세를 나누어 보기
lines: This is skiing in Riders Republic. Watch the tilt of the body and skis.
Read forward movement separately from changes in body orientation.
In the air, the travel path continues while facing and bank also change.
Remaining near screen center does not imply an unchanged orientation; the camera follows too.
We are learning a representation that can describe the visible motion, without claiming to have inspected the game code.
Our next diagram will hold position fixed and rotate the three body axes to isolate orientation.

scenes.title: 네 성분은 네 회전 각도가 아니다
lines: A quaternion contains one scalar and a three-component vector. We write components in w,x,y,z order.
A unit rotation quaternion has squared components summing to one, leaving three continuous degrees of freedom.
Four numbers are not four rotation angles, and x,y,z are not Euler angles.
The algebra uses i,j,k, whose squares each equal minus one.
The product ij is k, whereas ji is minus k: an early hint that order matters.
A library may store x,y,z,w instead. Check the named components and memory order.

scenes.title: 축·각에서 반각으로 연결하기
lines: Recall a unit axis and the angle of rotation about it.
The scalar is cos of the half-angle, and the vector is the unit axis times sin of the half-angle.
At zero angle, cos is one and sin is zero, giving the identity [1,0,0,0].
A 90-degree z rotation uses a 45-degree half-angle, so w and z are both sqrt(2)/2.
The half-angle does not mean half the physical rotation. Multiplication on both sides produces the full angle.
We retain right-handed column-vector conventions, and use radians in trigonometric calculations.

scenes.title: 몸에 붙인 축과 공중 회전
lines: Compare body facing when the skis leave the ground and when they land.
Imagine three small body axes; all of them rotate together in the air.
One direction alone cannot describe both body facing and ski bank.
A quaternion is one way to store the full orientation, not position or velocity.
We are not measuring exact axes and angles from the screen. We will define those explicitly in the next calculation.
Watch orientation separately from travel direction around landing to connect the representation to visible motion.

scenes.title: 구십 도 회전을 두 번 합치면
lines: Multiply the z90 quaternion by itself, applying the same rotation twice.
The new scalar is the product of scalars minus the vector dot product, which is zero here.
The two cross scalar-vector terms sum to a z component of one; the other components remain zero.
The result [0,0,0,1] represents z180.
After two more such rotations, the result is [-1,0,0,0], with the body back at its initial orientation.
The scalar changed from one to minus one, yet the orientation matches. Let us examine this double representation.

scenes.title: q와 -q는 같은 자세
lines: The unit quaternions q and -q produce the same rotation matrix and endpoint orientation.
All four components change sign. This differs from conjugation, which changes only the vector signs.
In vector rotation, the signs on both sides cancel.
Component equality alone is therefore insufficient to test orientation equality.
Equivalent endpoints do not make every interpolation path between signed representatives equivalent.
Endpoint orientation does not retain revolution count; store the path and accumulated rotation separately.

scenes.title: 같은 자세로 돌아와도 움직임은 남는다
lines: Follow the body forward direction and ski line through the airborne rotation.
A single frame cannot reveal the full movement that preceded it.
Time reveals the process; endpoint orientation and movement history are different information.
Connect this distinction to the two signed quaternions representing one orientation.
One quaternion does not automatically retain the number of visible revolutions.
If a trick needs accumulated rotation, track input or rotation history separately from orientation.

scenes.title: 항등원과 부호를 구분하기
lines: The multiplication identity is [1,0,0,0]; multiplying q by it leaves q unchanged.
[-1,0,0,0] is also the identity rotation, but is not the algebraic multiplication identity.
It changes q to -q: different components representing the same orientation.
An all-zero quaternion is not no rotation; it is a zero-norm invalid rotation input.
Initialize with the library identity constructor or correctly ordered unit components.
Distinguish equality as numbers from equality as rotations before reasoning about signs.

scenes.title: 길이와 정규화의 조건
lines: The norm is the square root of the sum of all four squared components, not just the vector norm.
Typical orientation storage and quaternion-to-matrix routines expect unit inputs.
For small floating-point drift, divide all four components by the norm.
Guard near-zero and nonfinite norms before division; do not disguise arbitrary invalid data as a valid rotation.
A nonzero nonunit quaternion can also rotate with its correct general inverse because scale cancels, unlike unit-assuming code.
Normalization restores the scale convention. It neither scales the rotation angle directly nor fixes wrong axes or multiplication order.

scenes.title: 속도 변화와 자세 저장값
lines: We will move from skiing to a flight segment. Watch movement speed separately from body orientation.
Faster motion does not mean a longer quaternion; a unit rotation retains norm one.
Speed and acceleration describe change, whereas orientation describes the current state.
The following camera moves as the wings bank. Apparent image size cannot reveal quaternion norm.
Check unit length in code or data; this footage is not a measurement of those values.
After observing motion, we will calculate how to undo a stored rotation in the next diagram.

scenes.title: 켤레로 단위 회전을 되돌리기
lines: Conjugation keeps the scalar and negates the three vector components.
For a unit rotation quaternion, the conjugate is the inverse and undoes the rotation.
Conjugating z90 preserves w and negates z, giving z minus90.
Their product returns [1,0,0,0].
Negating all four components instead gives the same orientation, not generally the inverse.
Special cases such as half-turns have matching inverse orientations, but conjugation and full negation remain different operations.

scenes.title: 일반 역원은 길이의 제곱으로 나눈다
lines: The general inverse is the conjugate divided by the squared norm, not the norm itself.
For [2,0,0,0], the norm is two and its square is four.
Dividing the conjugate by four gives [0.5,0,0,0].
Their product is the identity. Dividing by two would leave scalar two in the product and fail the inverse test.
For unit inputs the squared norm is one, recovering the conjugate rule.
The inverse requires a nonzero quaternion; reject zero and nonfinite inputs and inspect their origin.

scenes.title: 반대 회전과 되돌리는 과정
lines: Watch the snow bike bank and then adjust its orientation again.
Leaning one way and returning helps us visualize an opposing rotation.
The camera moves, so screen left and right do not determine exact axes or angles.
An inverse swaps the input and output of a stored rotation; it differs from riding backward or negating velocity.
Separating bank from travel shows why undoing orientation and undoing position are different questions.
Next we will diagram multiplication order and reference frames.

scenes.title: 내적과 외적으로 곱셈 읽기
lines: Consider the Hamilton product written in scalar-vector form.
Its scalar is the scalar product minus the vector dot product.
Its vector sums the two scalar-vector products and the vector cross product.
Reversing the cross product changes its sign, exposing the usual noncommutativity.
Products are associative, so parentheses can move without permitting arbitrary order changes.
Some rotations, such as those about one axis, do commute. Check the actual operation and convention.

scenes.title: 적용 순서와 곱셈의 좌우
lines: We use the Hamilton convention in which a vector rotates as q times v times inverse q.
Applying fixed x90 followed by fixed y90 puts the y quaternion on the left.
The initial z direction becomes minus y after x90 and remains there under y90.
In reverse order it becomes x after y90 and remains x under x90, so the results differ.
A world-frame delta premultiplies the current orientation; a body-frame delta postmultiplies it.
Check whether a library uses the same product convention, using small axis-rotation probes.

scenes.title: 동작 순서와 기준을 관찰하기
lines: We will observe snowboard jumps and then bike bank.
Changing the body forward direction also changes the direction of later body-relative motion.
Follow temporal order; an endpoint frame does not reconstruct every intermediate operation.
Distinguishing fixed world axes from moving body axes is the starting point for choosing multiplication side.
Following-camera pixels do not reveal the exact internal rotation order. Keep our defined diagram separate from observation.
Watch body facing together with the board or wheels to practice reading full orientation.

scenes.title: 두 자세 사이의 회전 차이
lines: Let a be the current and b the target local-to-world orientation.
A world delta must satisfy delta times a equals b, so it is b times inverse a.
A body delta postmultiplies a, giving inverse a times b. Changing frames changes the order.
From z30 to z90, the same-axis difference is z60.
With mixed axes, component subtraction is insufficient. Use inverse and product, and name the reference frame.
Apply the computed delta back to the current orientation and verify that it reaches the target.

scenes.title: 내적으로 최소 회전 각도 구하기
lines: The dot product sums products of all four quaternion components.
For the smallest physical relative rotation, take the absolute dot product.
Twice its arccos gives an angle from zero to 180 degrees.
Equivalent q and -q have dot minus one, whose absolute value gives zero rotation distance.
Validate unit inputs and clamp tiny numerical overshoot to [0,1] before arccos.
This measures minimal endpoint separation, not accumulated trick rotation or path direction.

scenes.title: 목표 자세와 가까운 자세
lines: Watch the board and bike adjust orientation toward landing after a jump.
The required change depends on the target orientation you choose.
Orientation difference is separate from the remaining positional distance.
Similar-looking screen poses still require rotation data for exact angle computation.
Minimal angle describes nearest endpoint separation, not the full length of the actual motion.
During a jump, follow both body facing and the wheel plane. Distinguish landing position from landing orientation.
Separate excerpts are not endpoints of the same jump. Observe each actual motion to frame the question about current and target orientations.
An inverse or relative rotation that matches a pose does not rewind position or collisions. Motion path and rotational endpoint are separate records.
Imagine comparing stored current and target orientations; next we will apply a chosen fraction of a rotation.

scenes.title: 회전의 일부를 적용하는 거듭제곱
lines: Given a chosen axis-angle representative, scale its angle while retaining its axis to form a fractional rotation.
Half of z90 is z45; this is not multiplication of all four components by 0.5.
A chosen logarithm stores the axis times half-angle as a pure quaternion, and the exponential reconstructs a unit quaternion.
Distinguish radians and the half-angle: the previous rotation vector used the full angle, whereas this logarithm uses half.
The power path depends on the selected sign and angle branch; fractional powers of q and -q can differ.
For a shortest path, choose the representative and boundary rules first, explicitly handling identity and half-turn ambiguity.

scenes.title: 벡터는 왜 양쪽에서 곱할까?
lines: In the complex plane, multiplication by cos(angle)+i sin(angle) rotates a 2D vector.
In 3D, one-sided multiplication of a pure-vector quaternion generally creates a scalar and is not a vector rotation.
For v=(1,0,1), left multiplication by z90 alone creates scalar minus sqrt(2)/2.
Including the inverse on the right restores scalar zero and gives vector (0,1,1).
The axis-parallel z component remains, while x rotates into y.
Both-sided multiplication combines two half-angles into the physical angle; a worked vector makes the structure tangible.

scenes.title: 카메라와 몸체가 함께 움직일 때
lines: Finally, observe the bike rotate in the air and land.
Facing and the wheel line change together; the camera is another reference that projects them onto the screen.
Separate making motion visible from computing orientation in world space.
With a stored quaternion, rotate direction vectors to obtain forward or up.
Pixels do not reveal the game storage format, but we can verify our defined mathematical example directly.
Now recheck component order and unit norm and solve the same calculation as an exercise.

scenes.title: 코드에서 확인할 약속
lines: Four float32 components occupy sixteen bytes of component data, excluding alignment and metadata.
One more number than Euler angles can make composition and interpolation convenient, without guaranteeing superior speed for every use.
Euler angles may suit human editing, while precomputed matrices may suit rotating many directions.
Check storage order, Hamilton product, handedness, and the local-to-world convention together.
Maintain normalization and invalid-input guards, and distinguish component equality from orientation equality.
A quaternion represents rotation; it does not automatically solve collision, translation, or accumulated rotation history.

scenes.title: 직접 돌리고 되돌려 보기
lines: First problem: rotate a vector ninety degrees about z. Its x is one, y is zero and z is one. What is the result? Pause and check the axes and signs.
Use [sqrt(2)/2,0,0,sqrt(2)/2] and the two-sided product on the pure vector.
The result is (0,1,1); x rotates into y and z remains. Length sqrt(2) is preserved.
Exercise two: should we negate all four components to restore the original vector?
No: use the unit conjugate, negating only the vector components. It restores (1,0,1).
Finally, decide whether an orientation difference is a world delta on the left or a body delta on the right.

scenes.title: 네 숫자에서 회전 연산까지
lines: A quaternion has four components formed from a unit axis and half-angle, with three rotational degrees of freedom under its unit constraint.
q and -q represent one orientation; conjugation serves a different role, and the general inverse divides by squared norm.
Record product order and reference frames for composition and differences, then verify by applying the result.
Next we will interpolate orientations smoothly and safely convert among quaternion, matrix, Euler, and other representations.
